editorial:
Imagine feeling so anxious that you have to write down every single thought just to keep your mind quiet. That is exactly what you see with Mayuko, a high school girl in Tokyo who spends her days juggling school and therapy while burning through stacks of notebooks. Her world is small and repetitive until her uncle Junpei suddenly shows up out of nowhere. You will find it really interesting how they bond because Junpei struggles with the same obsessive-compulsive habits. It creates a very sweet, quiet vibe as two lonely people find someone who actually understands their struggle without any judgment.

The acting feels very real and grounded, making you truly care about whether these two find peace. While the story moves slowly, it helps you feel the weight of their anxiety. The only downside is that it might feel too quiet for people who want big explosions or fast plots. If you enjoy deep character studies, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, you realize Junpei's mental state is much more fragile than Mayuko's. He eventually hits a breaking point where his rituals no longer help him cope. The twist is that while Mayuko uses her notes to move forward, Junpei becomes trapped by his own mind. In the end, Mayuko finds the strength to let go of her obsessive writing, using her bond with Junpei to finally find some inner peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching stories about family and mental health.
similarMovies: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
